headline: Arsenal held again in WSL; the rest stays rumour
paragraphs: The clearest fact of the day is a result, not a transfer. Arsenal's women drew 1-1 at home to London City Lionesses in the WSL on Sunday, their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season. Frida Maanum put Arsenal ahead before Isobel Goodwin equalised, and London City goalkeeper Mary Earps made the saves that held the point. Sky Sports and the Guardian both covered the match independently; the Guardian noted the draw does little for manager Renée Slegers's European qualification hopes.

Everything else touching the six clubs stayed at rumour level. Sunday's BBC gossip column reported Arsenal may have to pay RB Leipzig £66m for winger Antonio Nusa — also carried by BBC Sport, though that is the same newsroom rather than independent confirmation. Earlier in the week the same column linked Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi with a move to Atletico Madrid and put Real Madrid forward Endrick on Arsenal's radar, while Transfermarkt separately reported Real Madrid reviving interest in Michael Olise. None of these links were corroborated elsewhere.

Man City's only item was a single line from a Sky live blog: Erling Haaland said he 'hasn't read much' about the Premier League charges guilty verdict, with no further detail given. Liverpool's lone mention, via the same BBC column, was that right-back Jeremie Frimpong is not headed for the Anfield exit. There was nothing in today's feed specific to PSG or Bayern Munich, beyond a passing note that Barcelona are keen on Bayern defender Jonathan Tah.
